issues.description: The problem statement refers to a method named getFeedingSound() for the animal classes in multiple places (e.g., describing what Seal, Pig, and Goat should return), while the UML and the intended implementation use messageOnFeed(). This name mismatch in the specification vs. the implemented/expected method name can confuse students about which method to implement and call when feeding animals.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across the problem statement, template, and solution. Update the problem statement to refer to messageOnFeed() (instead of getFeedingSound()), or alternatively rename messageOnFeed() in the solution/template to getFeedingSound() so all artifacts consistently use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method as getFeedingSound(), while the UML and the solution/template use messageOnFeed(). This mismatch (getFeedingSound vs. messageOnFeed) refers to the same conceptual operation (the animal's feeding sound) but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students about which method to implement and call (e.g., implementing getFeedingSound() when the provided/skeleton code and solution expect messageOnFeed()).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the feeding-sound method across all artifacts. Prefer using messageOnFeed() everywhere (update the problem statement occurrences of getFeedingSound() to messageOnFeed()), or alternatively rename the abstract method in the UML/solution to getFeedingSound() and update implementation/signatures accordingly. Ensure examples, task descriptions, and feedAllAnimals() documentation consistently use the same method name.
